chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn Uqba from Sulayman ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"None of you should establish the Iqamah while walking, or riding, or lying down, unless he is ill, and he should steady himself in establishing the Iqamah as he steadies himself in the Salat, for indeed when he begins establishing the Iqamah, he is in Salat."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the posture of the person reciting the Iqamah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the reciter of the Iqamah must stand firmly, mirroring the stability of the one leading prayer, unless ill, thereby elevating the Iqamah recitation to a state of Salat. This ruling underscores the spiritual gravity of the Iqamah, treating it not merely as a call but as an act of worship requiring physical composure and presence of mind. The emphasis on 'stability' (tamakkun) reflects the Shia jurisprudential focus on the dignity and reverence due to the words of the muezzin.
